answer:
Neither option as posed. Assert the relationship — but assert it as the activity that mediates it, not as an arc between the two Persons, and do not leave it to be recovered by joining forty tapes.

1. There is no direct fiddler-to-fiddler property to assert. `connect E39 E39` returns nothing but L54 is same as. `connect E21 E21` returns exactly one declared person-to-person property, P152 has parent — and the tool prints its Full path through E67 Birth (P98i was born, P96 by mother / P97 from father). That is the CRM's pattern: even the most intuitive direct relation between two people is licensed only as a shortcut standing for a fully articulated path through an event (Introduction > Applied Form > Shortcuts). Nothing in the model declares a path for 'taught' or 'learned from', so there is nothing for a direct arc to stand for. The SIG did consider adding one and declined: Issue 256 (groups and relations between persons) was closed in Heraklion 2017 holding that the social relations prosopography explores go beyond the scope of CRMbase, and deferring them to a possible CRMsoc — and CRMsoc in that form was discontinued in Bern, April 2025 (Issue 580). Christian-Emil raised your exact case in t0834, using a student/teacher relationship from ULAN as the example that E74 Group cannot carry; Martin's reply named the category it belongs to — a relationship mediated by a continued activity — and floated an activity-mediated relationship class that was never adopted. It was never adopted because in CRMbase the mediating activity already is the representation.

2. But 'only inferred by chaining the forty sessions' is also wrong, for three reasons. (a) The forty sessions document co-participation, not teaching. P11 had participant and P14 carried out by carry no direction; forty joins establish only that the pair played together forty times, which is equally consistent with two peers swapping tunes. The asymmetry — who taught whom — is knowledge the archive holds from the family, and if it is not written down it is simply not in the catalogue. (b) The relationship is not the sum of the sessions. If a forty-first tape surfaces, or one is lost or re-dated, the relationship does not change; a relation whose only representation is a join over surviving evidence is fragile in exactly the direction the Monotonicity principle warns against. This is the same objection Franco pressed in t1701 — an intangible tradition is not the cumulation of its performances. (c) A forty-way path is not something a catalogue user can query.

3. What to build. Instantiate the apprenticeship once, as a single instance of E7 Activity: 'the teaching of the granduncle's repertoire to the grandnephew'. P2 has type an E55 Type such as 'oral transmission of repertoire / instruction'; P4 has time-span the three years; P7 took place at the kitchen; P14 carried out by the granduncle with P14.1 in the role of teacher, and P14 carried out by the grandnephew with P14.1 in the role of learner — P14 implies causal responsibility and the nephew was an active participant, and P14.1 supplies precisely the direction a bare 'learned from' arc would have carried. (Use P11 had participant for the nephew instead if the archive prefers to keep him passive.) The forty sessions are forty further instances of E7 Activity, each P9i forms part of that whole (P9 consists of downward), each with its own P4 has time-span taken from the tape's date. The catalogue then points at one node for the relationship, and the forty sessions survive as its documented parts rather than as its only trace.

The licence for treating forty events as one Activity is the SIG's own approved example. Under Issue 518 the Lerna IV-V settlement activity was voted in as an E7 Activity because the sources justify regarding it as one activity with a distinct identity and unity, with the looser archaeological periods left as E4 Period (t1471). One teacher, one pupil, one kitchen, one purpose, unbroken weekly for three years is as unified as an activity gets — quite unlike the 'All Tango Performances' aggregate Martin rejected in t1701 for having no clear identity, unity and distinction from others. E4 Period is the fallback only if the archive doubts the intentional unity, and here the intention is the one thing that is not in doubt.

4. Keep the evidence chain separate from the historical claim. Each recording is an instance of E31 Document (its scope note admits audiograms among the means of expressing propositions) and P70 documents the session it captured. That way a re-dating or re-attribution of one tape touches only a P70 arc and never the assertion of the apprenticeship.

5. Only if the archive is unwilling to assert the teaching in its own voice — defensible, since no lesson plan or tune list survives and the account came in with the donors — wrap it: an E13 Attribute Assignment, P14 carried out by the archivist or the donating family as informant, P140 assigned attribute to the grandnephew, P141 assigned the granduncle, P177 assigned property of type a 'taught by' E55 Type, P16 used specific object the tapes. The E13 scope note is explicit that this device marks the maintaining team as neutral to the assertion's validity and registers whose opinion it was, and equally explicit that the team's own assertions must not each be wrapped this way. So E13 is the right tool for the attributed reading and the wrong tool for the default one.

6. One part of the request the CRM will not carry: 'his repertoire'. With no tune list there are no identifiable instances of E73 Information Object to point at, and the model gives you no way to say that an unspecified set of tunes passed. You can type the activity's purpose (P21 had general purpose an E55 Type 'transmission of fiddle repertoire') but you cannot itemise, and you cannot say that the nephew's version of a tune derives from the uncle's. That is Issue 527 (modelling provenance of intangible heritage), still Open, where Martin observed that procedural and musical traditions would need a specific activity of transferring such knowledge plus a core-variant relation or variant set that the model does not yet have. Record the relationship; leave the repertoire's content to a free-text note until 527 resolves.

rejected_alternatives.option: A direct 'learned from' property between the two instances of E21 Person, as the primary record
rejected_alternatives.why_not: connect E21 E21 offers only P152 has parent, and the tool prints its Full path through E67 Birth; the CRM sanctions a direct arc only as a shortcut over a declared longer path. No path is declared for teaching, so there is nothing for such an arc to abbreviate. It is acceptable only as a locally derived convenience computed over the E7 Activity path, never as the stored record.

It is the only declared person-to-person property, but it covers biological or legally equivalent parenthood only, and the pair are granduncle and grandnephew, not parent and child. It is also a shortcut over E67 Birth, not over any teaching event, so it cannot be repurposed.

rejected_alternatives.option: E74 Group holding the pair, with the roles carried on membership
rejected_alternatives.why_not: This was the SIG's older workaround (the summary of t0426 records membership-role properties approved as shortcuts over E85 Joining events), and t0834 opens by challenging it for exactly this case: a teacher and a pupil are not a corporate actor and have no potential to act as one. A group node also has no time-span for the teaching, no place, and no link to the tapes.

rejected_alternatives.option: A Formal Social Binding class of the kind proposed for CRMsoc in t1169
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Its draft scope note requires the binding to come into being through an explicit act of declaration and to carry characteristic rights and obligations under a legal system — memberships, marriage, parenthood. A kitchen-table apprenticeship has no declaring act and no rights attached. It was in any case never adopted, and CRMsoc in that form was discontinued under Issue 580.

rejected_alternatives.option: E4 Period for the three years, without an E7 Activity
rejected_alternatives.why_not: It would carry the coherence but not the intention or the named agents; E4 has no P14 carried out by. Issue 518 settled that where identity and unity are evident the more specific E7 is the right choice, and here the deliberate teaching purpose is the best-documented thing about the case.

rejected_alternatives.option: CRMinf I5 Inference Making with I2 Belief nodes
rejected_alternatives.why_not: It is available and would genuinely trace the conclusion back to the tapes as primary evidence, which is what its scope note is for. But an I5 premise must be an I2 Belief, so it means minting belief nodes for each tape's content, and the archive is not adjudicating competing scholarly inferences — it is recording one family account. E13 Attribute Assignment gives the attribution at a fraction of the cost; escalate to CRMinf only if rival accounts of who taught whom appear.

rejected_alternatives.option: E65 Creation for the repertoire the nephew acquired
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Nothing conceptual was brought into existence: the tunes pre-existed both men. E65 would misdescribe transmission as origination, which is the distinction Issue 527 is still trying to model.

siblings_considered.why_not: It is tempting to treat the lessons as bringing the nephew's repertoire into existence, but E63 Beginning of Existence needs a persistent item that P92 brought into existence, and the archive cannot name one — the tunes already existed and no tune list survives to identify them. E63 also carries no requirement of intentional action, which would lose the deliberate teaching that is the whole point of the record.

E74 Group requires actors that act collectively or in a similar way through some unifying relationship, and the SIG's reading is that a group is itself one Actor. The granduncle and grandnephew are two individuals in an asymmetric teaching relation; treating them as a group would erase the direction that is exactly what the archive wants to record. Christian-Emil made this objection about student/teacher pairs in t0834.

E29 Design or Procedure is the class for documented plans for executing actions, which is what a lesson plan or a graded tune list would have been — and the case states that none survives. The tapes are records of what happened, not prescriptions for it, so they fall under E31 Document with P70 documents, not E29.

One could model the archivist's work as an E65 Creation producing a catalogue record. That documents the making of the record but not which relation was asserted between which two entities. Only E13, with P140 assigned attribute to, P141 assigned and the required P177 assigned property of type, makes the asserted relation itself queryable and attributable, which is the point of wrapping it at all.

notes:
I have kept classes_proposed to the four the question actually turns on. Two routine additions are needed to instantiate the model and are named in the answer rather than proposed: E52 Time-Span (required by P4 on every E7) and E55 Type (the range of P2, P21, P177, P14.1). The forty physical cassettes as instances of E22 Human-Made Object, and the donation itself as E10 Transfer of Custody, are real cataloguing work but sit outside the question asked, so I left them out.

What the tools made hard: the issue register and the docs section paths are not accepted by `search.py quote` (only threads, messages, episodes and document chunk ids are), so the wording of the Issue 256 and Issue 518 outcomes and of the E4/E31 scope notes could not be verification-checked. I read all of it in `issue` and `concept` output and have paraphrased it without quotation marks rather than quote unverified strings. `docs` does not print chunk ids, so a specific paragraph of the Shortcuts section cannot be cited more precisely than by its section path.

One honest limit beyond the answer: the CRM will represent the apprenticeship but not the repertoire that passed through it. Issue 527 is still Open on precisely that, and my recommendation deliberately leaves the tune-level content in free text.
